verdicts: The world is a fair test: an informed entity survives at least twice as well as chance; an entity that only sits in the dark room dies of boredom in at least 90% of worlds; an entity that only sits in the noise dies in at least 90% of worlds, mostly from failed prediction
informed 0.0 vs chance 21.7 deaths per 10k; dark-only dies of boredom in 100%; noise-only dies in 100% (100% from failed prediction)
Listening to boredom keeps the prediction-only entity alive better than ignoring it (deaths per 10k, ALL minus IGN below 0)
An entity that ignores boredom dies mostly OF boredom (more than half of its deaths come from the hidden need)
Listening to boredom keeps the hidden need fuller in the second half of life (ALL minus IGN above 0)
The prediction-only entity survives at least twice as well as chance (median deaths per 10k at most half of chance's)
The original drive, surprise minimisation, dies more than learning progress does (UR minus LP above 0)
Feeling only vitality and boredom is nearly as good as being handed the learning-progress drive with optimism (upper end of ALL minus LPO below 10 deaths per 10k)
Listening to boredom keeps the entity out of the dark room (share of time in the dark room, ALL minus IGN below 0)
